newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close lower despite HK Telecom gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close lower despite HK Telecom gains.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed lower on Friday ahead of the long weekend, unsettled by placement rumours and a ban on equity investment by Chinese banks and despite Hongkong Telecom's record-setting jump, brokers said.
"News from China that the central bank was stopping banks investing in stocks pulled the market down in the afternoon," said Peter Lui in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.

The Hang Seng Index closed 140.39 points lower at 14,655.13 after trading in a 366-point range during the day. The index jumped some 180 points early in the morning session, then lost 186 points at the start of afternoon trade.
Turnover was a very heavy HK$21.69 billion, but less than Thursday's HK$22.55 billion.
The Hong Kong stock exchange will be closed on Monday to mark the Dragon Boat Festival and resume normal trading on Tuesday.
Late on Thursday, the People's Bank of China issued a directive banning Chinese state banks from trading on the stock market and giving them 10 days to unwind their market positions.
The announcement sent the Shanghai A share index down 89.498 points or 6.30 percent and the Shenzhen A share index plunging 32.28 points or 6.83 percent, and affected sentiment in Hong Kong as well.
But brokers said the measures appeared to be aimed at curbing speculation in China's domestic stock markets and should have little concrete impact on Hong Kong.
China-backed red chips underwent profit-taking in the last hour of trade on Friday. Newcomer Beijing Enterprises shed HK$1.25 to HK$50.25 on heavy trade of HK$638 million.
China Everbright-IHD slipped HK$0.90 to HK$16.70, while Theme International added HK$0.875 to HK$5.10.
The companies confirmed they were negotiating an asset swap which could lead to Theme taking over Everbright-IHD's Singapore retail operations and Everbright-IHD taking a stake in Theme.

Most blue chips, with the exception of some banks, were hit by rumours that a major conglomerate may tap the market for funds. Hutchison fell HK$2.00 to HK$61.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties tumbled HK$4.25 to HK$92.75.

Hongkong Telecom was the one bright spot on renewed speculation that China may take a stake in the company. The share was the day's most actively traded, hitting an all-time high of HK$19.25 before ending up HK$1.90 at HK$19.00.
Hongkong Telecom said on Friday parent Cable and Wireless was in talks with Chinese authorities, but gave no details and warned the likely effect on itself was not certain.
